item.title: 'Only winter will come': Bangladesh minister doubts Hasina will return in December
item.description: Bangladesh's state minister for foreign affairs Humaiun Kobir expressed doubt over Sheikh Hasina's reported December return, saying only winter would arrive. He insisted that the former PM could be brought back from India only through the extradition treaty and in handcuffs or under strict surveillance to face trial. Hasina has reportedly sought a state aircraft to return on December 16.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: 'I'd like to have him': Trump on Putin's possible G20 visit amid Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump said that Vladimir Putin may join the G20 summit if he decides to do so. Trump highlighted the vital role of diplomacy in addressing the ongoing Russia-Ukraine crisis. Trump also said Putin wanted to reach an agreement to end the Russia-Ukraine war, arguing that maintaining a cordial relationship with the Russian leader was important to negotiations.
item.dc:creator: Kanchan Yadav

item.title: Five years after former farmland on England's Isle of Wight was left to recover, wildlife monitors report bird numbers almost tripling, butterfly counts rising 117% and bumblebee abundance increasing 64%
item.description: Wildlife recovery has been observed on the Isle of Wight after five years of rewilding efforts. Bird populations at Wilder Little Duxmore nearly tripled, indicating a significant resurgence. Meanwhile, butterfly counts at Wilder Nunwell increased by 117% and bumblebee abundance rose by 64%. Improvements in soil and water quality were also noted, showing the effectiveness of rewilding processes. This recovery highlights nature's potential when given the opportunity to regenerate naturally.
item.dc:creator: World Desk

item.title: 'Nuclear holocaust' risk: Trump claims Iran missiles can reach Europe
item.description: US President Donald Trump expressed concerns about Iran's missile capabilities and the prospect of regional instability. He stated that Iran could potentially launch nuclear attacks on Israel and surrounding countries in the Middle East. Trump emphasized the necessity of achieving peace in the region while supporting local countries until they can defend themselves. He noted that Iran does not currently possess a nuclear weapon, which is significant under international agreements.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Danish king’s 1495 flagship wreck yields medieval chain mail, raising questions about its soldiers
item.description: Recently, underwater archaeologists made a fascinating discovery: well-preserved fragments of medieval chain-mail armor found near an ammunition-tool chest. This remarkable find sheds light on the soldiers and military gear that were present on the Griffin, which tragically sank in 1495. With the armor's notable quality, researchers are keenly examining its historical implications.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: New York mother sought land back from daughter after 2012 transfer; appeals court upheld daughter's ownership
item.description: A New York mother transferred four parcels of land to her daughter during financial difficulties in 2012. The mother attempted to reclaim three properties after her daughter planned to sell them in 2024. The court upheld the daughter's ownership, concluding that the transfer was an outright gift without any promise of return. Although the mother maintained some involvement with the properties, this did not imply retained ownership.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Cairo fuel tanker inferno: Driver suspect held after explosion left 31 dead
item.description: After the tragic incident in Cairo, where fuel tanker overturned and ignited, resulting in 31 fatalities and injuring 26 others. The driver, just 21 years old, is being held for questioning as authorities investigate potential drug influence at the time of the crash. Forensic teams are actively working to identify the remains of the deceased while families utilize social media to locate their missing loved ones.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: 'Record-setting error': Trump claims fake GDP data before midterms, demands probe
item.description: Donald Trump expressed concerns over revised GDP figures, claiming they were previously misrepresented before the midterm elections. He called for an investigation into what he described as a record-setting error in the reported figures. Additionally, he criticized various groups, including immigrants and Minnesota's Somali population, suggesting they contribute negatively to the country. Moreover, he defended ongoing renovations at the White House, emphasizing the need for maintenance due to its age.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: 'Very strange': Zelenskyy questions Trump's Putin bonhomie, US support for Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy voiced serious concerns regarding US President Donald Trump's close ties with Vladimir Putin, whom he labeled an aggressor resembling Hitler. He expressed disappointment over Trump's positive remarks about Putin while Ukraine faces ongoing conflict. In contrast, Trump described Putin as a friend who genuinely seeks to end the war, revealing the complexities both leaders face in resolving this crisis.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Oregon family renovates free abandoned mobile home for $14k so mom and twins host Thanksgiving
item.description: An Oregon family took on the challenge of revamping a deserted mobile home into a cozy space for their relatives. Lyman Branson II and his family poured months of effort into fixing the property for Betty Branson and her daughters. Despite budget hurdles, they created a safe haven. Just in time for Thanksgiving, they received the occupancy certificate, allowing them to celebrate their first holiday together in their new home.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio court says lawyers must prove fair fees after client secures $250,000 car settlement herself
item.description: Amber Kopanski settled her car crash claim directly with Progressive Direct Insurance Company for $250,000 after parting ways with her lawyers. Her former law firm, Rumizen Weisman Co., Ltd., sought payment for its legal fees and costs after her settlement. The appeals court ruled that the firm cannot simply apply its contract percentage for payment determination.

item.title: Florida couple’s claim of toxic mould, snake in daughter’s bedroom gets fresh hearing after appeals court ruling
item.description: A Florida couple, William and Ashley Merryman, reported significant damage to their home and health risks. After filing a lawsuit, they sought a preliminary injunction against state agencies linked to environmental changes. The district court initially denied their request, citing delayed action and potential financial remedies. However, the appeals court found faults in the lower court's reasoning and has remanded the case for reconsideration.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In September, the first confirmed natural sea turtle nests on the US West Coast were found
item.description: In a historic first for Southern California, two olive ridley sea turtle nests were discovered in September 2026. Due to an imminent tropical storm, the eggs were carefully relocated and monitored at the Aquarium of the Pacific. On November 14, 54 hatchlings emerged and were released into the ocean, followed by another 21 from a second nest on Huntington Beach the next day.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Florida court overturns fraud findings in $34.7m tobacco death case, orders new damages trial
item.description: In a significant development, Frances Bessent-Dixon's lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds was impacted by a recent court ruling. The appeals court dismissed the prior jury's fraud verdict, necessitating a new trial focused on damages. Tyrone M. Dixon, Bessent-Dixon's late husband, passed away from throat cancer caused by smoking, with R.J. Reynolds asserting that he was aware of the dangers of tobacco.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: An Ohio lawyer denied partnership over gender wins $2 million award upheld after 9-year legal fight
item.description: In a landmark ruling, Pamela Pantages, a lawyer from Ohio, has triumphed in her discrimination lawsuit against her previous employer. The Eighth District Court of Appeals upheld a $2 million jury award, affirming her allegations of being denied partnership due to age and gender bias, as noted in the firm's owner’s comments. This decision corroborates the jury's findings of sex discrimination and contract breaches at The Becker Law Firm.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: South African father-son duo build record-breaking drone reaching 408 mph
item.description: On December 11, 2025, Mike and Luke Bell shattered records by piloting their Peregreen V4 quadcopter to an astonishing average speed of 408.60 mph, making it the fastest battery-powered quadcopter in history. This remarkable achievement resulted from their dedication to innovative design and rigorous testing, employing advanced aerodynamics and cutting-edge 3D printing techniques. It is a monumental step forward in the realm of drone racing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 28 ancient Gallic coins and skull fragments hint at lost sanctuary in France
item.description: Archaeologists exploring Bure in northeastern France uncovered 28 ancient Gallic coins alongside human skull fragments. The site is believed to be a Late Iron Age sanctuary used by the Leuci. In addition to the coins, a miniature bronze wagon wheel was also found, suggesting ritual significance. The discovery contributes to understanding the cultural and religious practices of ancient Gaul. Ongoing studies aim to clarify the site's history and purpose.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Jolly Cheery’s Journey: Tree travels with low-emission transport; tradition links Norway and Britain
item.description: This year, London welcomes a spectacular 21-metre Norwegian spruce named Jolly Cheery for its Christmas display. Selected through public voting, this tree represents the enduring friendship between Norway and the UK. To minimize environmental impact, it will be transported in an eco-friendly manner and adorned with energy-efficient lights, set to be unveiled on December 3. Post-Christmas, it will be composted, promoting sustainability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
